summary: A multi-agent pipeline for LLM-generated collider-physics analysis code: a helper selector picks domain helper functions, a generator writes Python, an execute-and-repair loop fixes runtime errors, a tracer maps task-card items to code, a critique agent flags mismatches, and a 'Golden Axe Oracle' flags ambiguities in the user's task card before generation. Validated on five hand-built LHC analysis task cards with Qwen and Llama open models.

claims.claim: Modular task decomposition enhances transparency and reliability relative to the previous single-prompt approach
claims.evidence: No quantitative head-to-head with the earlier single-prompt system; §4.3 presents only Case 5 in detail ('qualitative patterns are similar'), with Table 3 a manual author judgment of four generated programs (2 pass, 2 partial success).

claims.claim: Enables substantially smaller (~14B) models to run the complete workflow
claims.evidence: §5 states the previous implementation needed ~70B; §4.3 shows Qwen3-14B codegen produced partial successes (wrong composite Delta-phi) when helpers were chosen by the 14B selector. 'Runs end to end' is supported; 'correct' is not.

claims.claim: Ambiguity oracle detects useful specification ambiguities before code generation
claims.evidence: Table 4: counts of useful vs off-target ambiguity detections over ten runs per model (e.g. 27 useful for Qwen2.5-7B); categories defined and judged by the authors, no ground-truth ambiguity set or second rater.

claims.claim: Explicit composite-object definitions in the task card improve generation stability
claims.evidence: §4.1 asserts 'significantly improved generation stability' from preliminary studies; no numbers reported.

patterns.note: Role-separated generation, execution, tracing, critique agents; no ablation against fewer roles.
Structured task cards with explicit object definitions; claimed to help, not measured.
Pre-generation ambiguity detection on the spec, with alternative readings returned to the user.
Execute-and-repair loop catches runtime errors; authors stress it does not catch semantic errors.
LLM critique agent compares as-implemented spec to task card; not validated against ground truth.

methodology.sample: Five collider-physics task cards; detailed results for one (Case 5)
methodology.baselines: None quantitative; refers to authors' previous CoLLM single-prompt system
methodology.models: Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen3-14B, Llama3-70B, Qwen2.5-7B (oracle); codegen switched to Qwen3-14B because Qwen2.5-14B API became unavailable
methodology.variance: Helper selection 5 runs; oracle 10 runs; codegen outputs judged once
methodology.ablations: Helper-card source varied (14B vs 70B selector); no component ablation

standards.artifacts: Package said to be on GitHub; no URL extracted in signals

biases.detail: Authors judge their own pipeline's outputs manually (Table 3) and label oracle detections as useful/off-target.
Five task cards, one reported in detail.
Case 5 chosen as 'representative' without reporting the other four.
Hand-written benchmark analyses rather than real published analyses.
Critique and tracer outputs are not validated against independent ground truth.

coi.affiliations: KIAS (Korea); KEK Theory Center, Sokendai, Kavli IPMU (Japan)
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None; open-weight Qwen and Llama models used. The regex 'Oracle' hit refers to the 'Golden Axe Oracle' module, not Oracle Corp.

verdict_reason: off-topic: LLM code generation for collider-physics analyses, with evaluation of five hand-built task cards judged manually by the authors and no quantitative comparison to the prior system. The ambiguity-detection idea is tangentially relevant to spec-driven development, but the evidence is too thin to inform a harness decision.
applicability: Little transfer to a Java backend team. The one portable idea is a pre-generation 'ambiguity pass' over a spec that lists unclear phrases with two candidate readings for a human to choose, and a post-generation trace mapping each spec item to the code that implements it. Both resemble spec-driven review steps the team could try on ingestion rules (e.g. which content items a filter applies to, in what order validations run), but this paper offers no measured evidence they help, and its domain, Python stack and small open models do not match.
